questions.q:
I have nobody_______I can confide in.

[CPO Tier II - 26/07/2021]
questions.s:
Correct Answer: whom

In this sentence, "whom" is used because it refers to the person you can confide in (the object of the action).

Correct Sentence:I have nobody whom I can confide in.

"Whom" is used for the person you are talking about (as the object of the action).

"Which" is used for things, not people.

"Whose" shows possession (something belonging to someone).

questions.q:
The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.

The man whose sitting at the corner table is my uncle.
questions.s:
The erroneous part is 'whose sitting'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'who is sitting' should be used instead of 'whose sitting'.
  • 'Who' is a subject pronoun that is used to describe who performed an action or who is in a specific state.
  • 'Whose' is a possessive pronoun that refers to the person to whom something belongs.
  • Here, in the given sentence 'who' is referring to the subject 'the man'.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.
     

Correct Sentence: The man who is sitting at the corner table is my uncle. 

Hinglish 

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहां 'whose sitting' के स्थान पर 'who is sitting' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
  • 'Who' एक subject pronoun है जिसका उपयोग यह वर्णन करने के लिए किया जाता है कि किसने कार्रवाई की या किसी विशिष्ट स्थिति में कौन है।
  • 'Whose' एक possession pronoun है जो उस व्यक्ति को संदर्भित करता है जिसके पास कुछ है।
  • यहाँ, दिए गए वाक्य में 'who' विषय 'the man' की बात कर रहा है।
  • अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

questions.q:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

______ of the two contestants was willing to withdraw from the tournament.
questions.s: The correct answer is 'Neither'. 'Neither' refers to not one out of the two in a group, while 'none' refers to not even one in a group of more than two things. We use neither of with a singular verb when it is the subject. Example: Neither of my best friends was around.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

When Sanathan asked Mr. Jignesh / for a fresh evaluation of his performance / in the last financial year, / little did him know that the results will come out worse than expected.
o: for a fresh evaluation of his performance
little did him know that the results will come out worse than expected
questions.s:
The sentence contains a pronoun error. The objective pronoun 'him' should be replaced with its subjective pronoun 'he' as the verb 'know' requires a subject. Therefore, the error is in the part in option (d).

The correct sentence is: When Sanathan asked Mr. Jignesh for a fresh evaluation of his performance in the last financial year, little did he know that the results will come out worse than expected.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions: Anjali drove us home.

Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party.

questions.q: Q16. 16. After a long and fun-filled day, the children slept themselves peacefully.
questions.s: 'Sleep' intransitive verb hai, iske sath reflexive pronoun nahi lagta. Do not use reflexive pronouns with 'sleep'.

questions.q:
My sister and myself are pleased to accept your invitation to dinner.

(SSC Stenographer Grade C&D-05/02/2019)
questions.s:
The correct answer is "My sister and I".

The error lies in the use of "myself". "Myself" is a reflexive pronoun, used for emphasis or to refer back to the subject (e.g., "I did it myself"), but it should not be used as the subject of a sentence.

The correct form here is "I" because it is the subject of the sentence along with "my sister."

Correct sentence: My sister and I are pleased to accept your invitation to dinner.

questions.s:
After “both,” we need subject pronouns when they act as the subject of the sentence.
Hence, “I” (not “me”) is correct here.
